newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker on IMM selling.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker on IMM selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3740 (US$0.7278) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3700 (US$0.7299) under pressure from selling on the International Monetary Market in Chicago and other U.S. investors, dealers said. * They said the currency should weaken further overnight, but sellers should hit resistance around C$1.3775 (US$0.7259).
Canada's dollar waned as the U.S. dollar rose despite efforts by German leaders to play down the recent rally against the mark.

Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the dollar and British pound had risen against the German mark because of strong economies in the United States and Britain and that currency market fluctuations were no grounds for worry.
Waigel's comments were interpreted as far more optimistic than investors expected and pushed the dollar higher.
"In essence, he was giving the green light to buy dollars," said John McCarthy, senior vice president at ING Barings.

Economic news added further strength to the U.S. dollar this morning after data released on U.S. consumer prices and industrial production offered fresh evidence of low inflation growth in the U.S. economy.
The U.S. government reported that CPI for the first half of 1997 rose a modest 2.4 percent, the lowest in 32 years, while manufacturing output rose faster than expected at 0.3 percent for June.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell against the German mark to 1.3048 marks from 1.3078 marks at Tuesday's close, and fell to 83.90 Japanese yen from 84.39 yen.
